items.response:
Two pages with different access: /pricing is public with plan content in a typed ts file, and /settings/team requires sign-in and lists org members. I'll check how routes are currently protected so the pricing page stays public and the team page gets the right guard.
Action: Look at the app's routing and auth/route-protection setup and how org members are fetched, then add both pages with a plans data file and tests.

I'll add `--since <date>` to `acme invoices export` and pass it through as the `since` query parameter, validating the YYYY-MM-DD format so a bad value fails with a clear message. Since this is a new CLI option, I'll also update docs/cli.md.
Action: Open the export command in packages/cli, add the option and validation, add a test, and update docs/cli.md.

I'll add `.nvmrc` at the root and an `engines` field in the root package.json, but I won't guess the Node major. The version in use should be visible in CI config, a Dockerfile, or what the repo runs on now.
Action: Check CI workflows, Dockerfiles and the current `node -v` for the version in use, then add `.nvmrc` and `engines` to match; if they disagree I'll ask you which one to standardize on.

You're welcome. The full web unit suite and the web typecheck are still running; I'll post the results when they finish.
Action: Wait for both to finish and report the results.

I'll add Storybook stories covering each Badge size, and run Storybook on port 6006 to check them. For Sam's question, I haven't looked, so I don't know yet whether clicks on the status filter are tracked, and I'll search instead of guessing.
Action: Find the Badge component and its size variants, add the stories, start `pnpm --filter web storybook`, and grep for analytics or tracking calls around the status filter to answer Sam.

Good, the team=payments tag guess stands then. For the trailmix double submit: disable the submit button while the request is in flight with `hx-disabled-elt="this"` on the button or form, and add `hx-sync="this:drop"` on the form so a second request is dropped while one is running. Since client-side guards can be bypassed, a unique constraint or dedupe check on the server is the robust fix.
Action: Share the htmx snippet for the form, and if you point me at the add-hike template and view I can apply it and add the server-side check.

I'll add one structured log line per org in the overdue reminder job showing what it decided (send or skip) and the reason for each skip, using the existing logger. I'll log org ids, not emails or other personal data.
Action: Read the overdue reminder job in the worker, add the per-org decision logging at each early return and skip, and add a test that checks the skip reasons are logged.

I'll fix the 'recieve' typo in the reports page empty state and grep the whole repo for other misspellings of recieve (recieve, recieved, recieving). There are earlier notes about the invoices empty state having a 'recieve' typo too, which the grep will catch. I'll only change user-facing text and comments, and list anything that's an identifier or a value other code might depend on instead of changing it.
Action: Run a case-insensitive grep for 'recie' across the repo excluding node_modules, fix the text occurrences, and report what I left.

I'll normalize the string to NFKD, strip the combining accent marks, lowercase it, replace each run of non-alphanumerics with a single dash, trim dashes from both ends, and cut to 64 characters without leaving a trailing dash. 'Café Müller' becomes 'cafe-muller'. I'll check whether the repo already has a slugify helper before adding one.
Action: Search for an existing slugify, otherwise add it in the shared lib folder with tests for accents, repeated separators, leading/trailing dashes and the 64-char cut.

The form and its `saveCompany` server action are written, with name and sender email required and a PATCH to /v1/org/profile. What's missing is the `settings/company/page.tsx` that loads the current profile and renders the form with those values.
Action: Create that page, check how the current org profile is fetched (I don't know if there's a GET on /v1/org/profile), render the form pre-filled, and add tests for the required-field validation.

I'll add retry with exponential backoff in the CLI api client, with up to 3 tries, only on 502, 503 and 504 responses, not on other errors like 4xx. One caution: retrying non-idempotent requests such as POST can create duplicates, so I'll flag how I handle those.
Action: Find the api client in packages/cli, add the retry wrapper, and write tests using fake timers so they don't wait on real delays.

I'll write an end-to-end test that drives a real browser through the full flow: new invoice, pick client, add a line, save, send. I don't know yet what e2e tooling the repo has, and I'd make sure the send step doesn't actually email a real customer.
Action: Check for existing e2e setup (Playwright or similar config and the dev server port), then write the test in that setup, with the send going to a local or mocked mail path.

I'll add msw as a devDependency in packages/cli, so the lockfile updates as well, and move the http mocking in the invoices tests onto its node server. Because #1192 is already open, I'll put this in a separate commit on the branch so the diff is easy to review.
Action: Run `pnpm --filter @acme/cli add -D msw`, convert the invoices tests to msw handlers, and run the CLI tests.

I'll add the duplicate button using the shadcn/ui Button from apps/web/components/ui with a lucide-react icon, not the hand-rolled icons. Since it's icon-only, it gets an aria-label like the trash button does (for example 'Duplicate line item <description>'), and the icon is aria-hidden.
Action: Open the line item row component, add the button next to the trash one with a handler that inserts a copy of the line, and add a test for it.

The common thread is that each of these imports is a type, written as a regular import, and with `verbatimModuleSyntax` on, TypeScript requires type-only imports to be written with `import type { ... }` or inline `type` modifiers. The list is cut off after the api routes, but the pattern in everything I can see is the same.
Action: Run the linter's autofix for consistent type imports if it has that rule, otherwise convert them in bulk, then rerun the typecheck across the monorepo.

`docker compose up -d` creates the containers, networks and volumes if they don't exist (recreating containers whose config changed) and starts them in the background. `docker compose start` only starts existing stopped containers, and doesn't create anything or pick up changes to the compose file. For first-time setup, like the contractor's, you want `up -d`.
Action: No action needed unless you want me to adjust the Slack message.

There is a real difference: `structuredClone` keeps Dates as Dates, supports Map, Set, typed arrays, undefined values, circular references, NaN and Infinity, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings and drops undefined values and breaks on circular references. The JSON trick is only worth it when you deliberately want a JSON-safe copy, and `structuredClone` throws on functions and DOM nodes.
Action: No action needed; tell me where you're using it if you want me to check a specific case.

Understood: from now on I'll test a change end to end before opening a PR, not just with unit tests, and I'll say what I ran. For the font change we just made, I'll load the app and check the font in a real browser rather than relying on the unit tests.
Action: Start the dev server and verify the Inter font with `display: 'swap'` and the `--font-sans` variable renders correctly in a browser, and report what I could and couldn't check (I may not have Safari).

I'll grep for 'recieved' in apps/api and services/worker and fix the spelling in comments, logs and strings. If one is a value in an API response, clients might compare against the exact string, so I'll list those for you instead of changing them.
Action: Run the grep across both directories, fix the text-only occurrences, run the worker and api tests, and report what I left.

I'll add an optional `memo` string with a max of 500 characters to the POST /v1/invoices request schema, using zod like the rest of runtime validation here. It also has to be stored and returned, so I'll check whether the invoices table already has a place for it, and add a column and migration if not. I don't know yet how the API docs are produced, so I'll check that to make sure memo shows up there.
Action: Find the invoice create schema and route, add the field with validation, the column and migration if needed, the response DTO, and the docs, with tests for 500 vs 501 characters.

I'll add a worker job that loads the org (scoped by orgId), skips it when callback_url is empty, and POSTs an invoice.paid event with a timeout, throwing on a non-2xx so the queue retries. Because queue redeliveries caused duplicate reminder emails before, I'll include a stable event id and make the delivery safe to repeat. Since callback_url is customer-controlled, I'll require https and avoid following redirects to internal addresses.
Action: Read the existing invoice-reminder job for the job and queue registration pattern, then write the new job with tests for the empty URL, success, and non-2xx cases.

An invoice should only show as Overdue if it's unpaid and past due, so a paid invoice should never get that badge. Your earlier note that the dashboard overdue badge counted drafts suggests the overdue rule isn't being applied by status consistently, so I'll use one shared rule for both. I'll check the real status values in the code first.
Action: Find the badge logic, restrict overdue to unpaid non-draft statuses, test paid, draft and voided with past due dates, and check the dashboard count uses the same rule.

Parking the timing work; I haven't written anything for it, and I'm still waiting on which framework the api uses. For the seed, random data with no uniqueness guarantee is the likely cause of duplicate emails, but I want to read the script before saying so.
Action: Read the seed script, find how customer emails are generated, and make them unique (for example by deriving them from a counter or index) with a re-run to confirm.

Two hours of roadmap slides will do that. Nothing is queued on my side, so take a break.
Action: Wait for what you'd like to pick up next, and I can start with something small.

I'll add a ServiceMonitor template to the worker chart in infra/helm/worker that scrapes the metrics port 9464 at /metrics, behind a values toggle so values.yaml and values-prod.yaml can control it. I need to check that the worker Service exposes a named port for 9464 and what labels your Prometheus uses to select ServiceMonitors, so Grafana really picks it up.
Action: Read the worker chart's service and values files, add templates/servicemonitor.yaml, and validate it with `helm template` and lint locally without applying anything.
